utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There are no preliminary matters. There are no issues to be dealt with by the Chamber. Therefore, we'll wait for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Milojica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you will tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Zec will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Zec, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Milojica.

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Yesterday we were looking at the record of your interview in 1993 that you provided to the investigative judge of the Banja Luka military court. Before which go any further, let me ask you this: When you appeared before the judge in 1993, he informed you why you were interviewed; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: At the beginning of the interview, the judge informed you about the criminal charges that you were facing and in which -- which, in fact, were read out to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think he did read that, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: The judge advised you of the right not to say anything in your defence or to -- or to answer any question; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't really remember that. I don't have a very good memory. I was wounded and quite affected by it all, so to tell you the truth, I really don't recall some things.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And you were advised of the right to a defence counsel to be present during the interview; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes. But I say again, I cannot remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: In fact, a defence counsel was assigned to you and he was present during the interview; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, I really cannot remember that a lawyer was present during that interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: His name was Radenko Jankovic. You remember the person who was present there during the interview?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: After the judge told you all of this, you said that you understood everything and that you wanted to give a statement in your defence; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did give a statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we can see -- see the document in front of us. It's not the order in which things happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, that is a matter for re-examination, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Mr. Zec, at the same time, of course, rather -- I don't remember, but rather be precise and accurate in this respect --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because Mr. Lukic will --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was misrepresented from the document. First, the witness -- okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic that's a matter for re-examination. If you think that Mr. Zec is not eliciting the evidence which you consider the accurate evidence, then you have an opportunity during re-examination. At the same time, I warn Mr. Zec that he should not be -- that it's rather for him at this moment not to create any confusion which you would then have to deal with at a later stage. Please proceed, Mr. Zec and, of course, it may be helpful to look at the document for the Chamber also.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. President. Can we have 65 ter 31697. Page 2 in both languages. Towards the bottom of the page it said that -- that the -- Mr. Milojica was informed of -- that there was a reasonable suspicion constituting grounds for charges against him. And then goes to the next page in both -- in -- also in the B/C/S. The accused was advised of the right not to say anything in his defence or answer any question. Then states that: "The accused was advised of the right to a defence counsel who can be present during the questioning. "After being advised all of the above, the suspect stated the following: I understand the charges and I will" --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It's not now for Mr. Zec. There is no B/C/S translation I am hearing from my colleagues and my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's the case -- of course, Mr. Zec only read apparently what is in the document but at the same time we should receive a B/C/S translation because he'll not continue doing that. Let me just check.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you want to know what I objected to, maybe it would shorten this. I objected that, first, the witness said that he understood everything, and then legal advisor was pointed. It was not vice versa as it was presented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. -- I said now twice that you can deal with the matter in re-examination. Mr. Zec now was reading what is said here, and -- Mr. Zec, you referred to the presence of a lawyer during the interview. If there's any specific portion you'd like to read which makes clear that a lawyer was not only appointed but present, then, of course, that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: In that respect, Your Honours, it's first line below that says "decision," that the counsel was appointed. At the last page, it refers to the defence counsel - last page in both versions - it refers to defence counsel stating that he had no more questions which shows that that counsel was present during the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think I wanted to avoid that we intervene during the cross-examination and that you had a reason to raise certain matters in re-examination, but since you've done it, now I'd like to know from you whether there's any reason why, at this moment, you think what was read by Mr. Zec makes clear that there was no lawyer present. He was appointed and he said at the end that he had no further questions. Now what's there what justifies your intervention?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The order of the facts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then it only strengthens my opinion and I'll -- I'll discuss this with my colleagues, that it would have been appropriate to deal with the matter in re-examination rather than to intervene. Because you may argue that if at the end someone says they have no more questions, he could not have been there on from the beginning. That's -- you can argue that. But it's at least not such a distortion of what the document says that it justifies an intervention. Please proceed, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Milojica, so the reality is you were informed of all of these rights even before you said a word to the judge; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: After the interview, you were offered to read the record of the interview; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't read any of it because, as I said, I was indisposed. I didn't really feel up to reading any of it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: First of all, you just said now and yesterday that you were threatened about and you were fearing of something, but last time when you were here testifying, you only said that you don't remember giving the statement, nothing -- no word about being threatened or anything. So now you are again changing your evidence, do you?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said it was not my statement, it is my signature, but it's not my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: It was read out loud and you signed the record without any objections; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that it was read out aloud. They were sitting farther away from me, and I really cannot remember any of it, if you believe me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I at this point in time put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you please explain who was it who threatened you to give this statement to the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Where did you meet them? Or were you in their custody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I was in custody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How many people -- policemen were with you at that moment, when you were threatened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there were three of them. And also one of them was there when I was giving the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did he threaten you while you were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. To stand against the wall, that I would be beaten, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did he say that to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Was in the presence of the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The one who was questioning me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did he hear that, what the military policeman was saying to you at that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I didn't receive interpretation. Can the answer be interpreted again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your answer. I asked you: Did he hear that, what the military policeman was saying to you at that moment? And I'm referring to the investigative judge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether he heard it or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How far away from you was the investigative judge sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. Perhaps some 4 to 5 metres away from me. It wasn't more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What exactly did the policeman in that room where you were interviewed say to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That I would probably receive a death sentence. I don't know, something like that. That I would be beaten. And then I was so frightened I completely lost all my composure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And that resulted in telling a detailed story about what happened to the priest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say this. I don't know how they drafted it. I don't know if they took the statement from somebody else and then they put into my statement whatever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to approach the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you please move a little bit closer to the microphone because your voice is very low. Thank you. Did you tell the investigative judge anything? Did you tell him any story or was it just put on paper and you signed it while you remained silent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did say what I said during the trial before, and then they were taking that down, and then they typed out the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which "trial before" are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I testified in the Karadzic trial here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That means you -- in that moment, when you were interviewed by the investigative judge, you told him a story. Was it just imagination what happened, or did you tell partly the truth or the whole truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And your evidence is that you told another story than that which was noted down; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you tell that the Chamber when you testified in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did say that this was not my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one additional question in that respect. Your lawyer just accepted that they read out a statement which was quite different from what you had told?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He did, yes. If I understood it correctly. I -- I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, a lawyer was present. You tell us that what they wrote down is quite different from what you had told the investigating judge. My question is whether your lawyer accepted that just a totally different story was put on paper and read -- and was read out or did he protest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He accepted what was written. He didn't object or -- or put any questions himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But didn't you then tell him not -- or to protest when your statement was distorted fully?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't dare say anything because I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you have said anything to your lawyer if you would have dared to ask him to protest against what was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, to the lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, at the same time, today you tell us that it wasn't read out, that you didn't read it, and you also tell us that you would have protested. But from what you told us until now, you were not even aware at that time, that what was put on paper was not your statement. So how could you tell us that you would have protested where you were not even aware and that it was just because you didn't dare to say anything, while at the same time you're telling us that you didn't know what was put on paper so that there was no reason for protest, whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know what was on the paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, it could not be out of fear that you did not protest and that you didn't ask your lawyer to protest because you were not aware.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, well, I didn't even know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, therefore, if you tell us that out of fear you didn't dare to ask your lawyer to protest, it's without any ground.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how to answer this. Again, I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you say that you -- on the one hand, you say you do not know what was put on paper, that it was different from what you had said. At the same time, you tell us that you didn't dare to ask your lawyer to protest against what was happening. But there was no fear because you didn't even know that something was put on paper which was different from what you had said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't even know what they wrote, and I didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, therefore, it could not be out of fear that you didn't ask your lawyer to protest against what was ongoing because you were not aware of what was ongoing, as you told us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to that. Mr. Zec, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Milojica, at the end of the statement it says after being advised of the contents of Article 82 of the Criminal Code -- Procedure Code, you stated that -- that you did not wish to read the record because it was dictated out loud and you would sign it without any objections. So now you saying that you did not know what is on the paper is just a lie, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a lie. I just signed it, and I said that I was scared and I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: You knew what is on the paper when you signed it; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I didn't say that you read it. It was read out, out loud --

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection. Again, it's not read out. It's dictated loud. It's here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, but the question has been asked and the question has been answered. Let's leave it to that. Now, what Mr. Zec is putting to you is the following. If we would believe you, the consequence is that the investigating judge is lying. He is putting something on paper which is totally wrong apparently intentionally, that the same is true for the court clerk who signed it, and that your lawyer was accepting this without any words. So there are three persons --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, please. There is no signature of the lawyer. That was our point. There was no signature of the lawyer. It has to be there [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm not in a -- Mr. Lukic, I'm not a debate with you. The witness said that something was put on paper in the presence of the lawyer. The lawyer not protesting --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the beginning he said that he does not remember the lawyer at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, we leave it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was presented to him [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- this is argument, Mr. Lukic, at this moment. Two or three people, but at least that there were basically lies and that you're the victim of that. That is what Mr. Zec is putting to you. Is that the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. To this day, I claim that this is not my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but there's more. But I leave it to that. By the way, Mr. Lukic, when I was addressing the witness, I was telling him what Mr. Zec put to him and that includes the presence of a lawyer. Please proceed, Mr. Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Your cousin Boro Milojica and Ranko Karan were also interviewed about the same time; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Apart from some details regarding the location where you met Ivica Pavlovic, Boro's and Ranko's statement were very similar to yours. You all blame Ivica for the murder; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't blame him. He admitted it himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: So regarding the murder, there is no dispute that you and your friends did take the priest to Ljubija and that you were there when the priest was shot. That is what you say in your 1993 statement, that's what you said in court when you were here first time. So there's no problem with that. You were there present during the murder; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the car. I did not see when Ivica shot him because he took him further away from the car.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all unnecessary microphones please be switched off when the witness is speaking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: You told the judge in 1993 in your defence that Ivica took a rifle from you and fired some 15 bullets into the priest; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't I didn't have a rifle at all. My rifle remained in Western Slavonia. After that I was wounded and I had no rifle at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: You told the judge that the rifle belonged to Boro, your cousin, that's what you said. It's not yours but Boro's, cousin, but you had in your hands before Ivica took it; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rifle was not in my hands. It was in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Let's look what you said in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: We have the statement, it's 65 ter 31697. We need page 3 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Towards the end of the page: "At that moment, Ivica Pavlovic took from me an automatic rifle and fired a burst of some 15 bullets at the priest. The rifle that I held belonged to Boro Milojica. When Pavlovic shot the priest, we asked him why he did it, and he answered: The dog did not deserve to live." This is what you told the judge in 1993 in your defence; yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection. Several times this witness claimed that this is not his statement so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So -- let's resolve in this way. Mr. Zec, the witness said several times that this is not his statement. So the appropriate way of asking the witness is confronting him with what the statement as put on paper says and ask for comment. Because if it's not his statement, it doesn't mean that in every respect it would not be -- reflect the truth because there are certainly some elements, as presence of the witness at the crime scene, which seems not to be denied by him. So, therefore, the appropriate way is not to say: "You said this," and et cetera, but then to say: "The statement reads that," and then you can ask the witness for any comment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Milojica, what I read to you is written in the record of the interview. So what is your comment about this event, the description of the event?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: The portion that I read to you that Ivica took rifle from you and shot the priest.

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't take the rifle from me. The rifle was in the car in the back, that thing, whatever it's called, back there in the car. It's a shelf or whatever. But I never held the rifle in my hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Your cousin Boro and Ranko told the judge the same thing, that Ivica grabbed the gun from you and shot the priest. I take it that you are aware of this?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they said. I said that I never held the rifle in my hands. The rifle was back there on that shelf in the car and he grabbed it from there. Perhaps that was misunderstood, that he had grabbed it or taken from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31697 receives number P6965, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. By the way, could the witness take off his earphones for a second. Could you take off your earphones for a second. Mr. Lukic, I'd like to briefly revisit your objections earlier. You brought to my attention that the witness initially would have stated that there was no lawyer present. Upon a specific question which I put to you, the witness said about the lawyer: "He accepted what was written. He didn't object or put any questions himself." If that is what the witness has testified, even if initially he would have said something different, then it's inappropriate when I put to the witness what Mr. Zec apparently wants to put to him, and which I heard myself at least in interpretation, that the witness stated about the behaviour of a lawyer who he didn't say was not present at that time but explained what he did and what he did not, that is, to put any additional questions. Then it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd rather not be interrupted. Then it is inappropriate, Mr. Lukic, to bring to my attention, without asking first that the witness takes off his earphones, to bring to my attention, and with that to the attention of the witness, that he initially stated that no lawyer was present. If you think - and I'm inclined to say that that would be a wrong thought - that you should intervene at that point, then at least you should have avoided that the witness would hear your intervention, and the way to do that is to ask me to invite the witness to take off his earphone. I leave it to this. The witness may put on his earphone again. And may this be of guidance for any future intervention, if needed at all. Mr. Zec, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Milojica, in 2006, your cousin Boro with whom were involved in this murder, he was on trial in Banja Luka for another murder that he had committed in August 1992 against a Muslim near Prijedor; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was tried for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And you appeared as a defence witness in that trial in 2006; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: You wanted to help your cousin on trial by offering evidence which was contrary to all other evidence that was presented in that case; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: The evidence in that case was that at the time of the crime your cousin Boro had a beard and you told the court that he did not; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said, and he did not have a beard. When I came from hospital, when he came to visit me, he had the kind of beard I had now. And as I said then, it was the kind of beard that can grow in, say, 20 days or a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 31700.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: This is the judgement in the case against your cousin Boro Milojica from 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have e-court page 6 for English and B/C/S page 9. On the top of the page, there is a -- there is your name. It says the witness, cousin of the accused, Milojica Ratko, and then the court provides summary of your evidence. And several lines below towards the middle of the page, the court said about your testimony the following: "The only fact negated by the witness is that Boro had a beard at the time in question. However, the court does not accept this part of the testimony as it is contrary to all other statements; it is the opinion of the court that the witness, who is related to Boro, is trying to describe Boro differently - as not having a beard." So, Mr. Milojica, the fact is that the court did not accept this and found that you wanted to help your cousin by providing false evidence; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They either did not understand me properly. I cannot see what is written here, but I said when I came from the hospital on the 22nd of July, Boro visited me on the 23rd and he didn't have a beard then. And I don't know when this happened, this killing, on which date and how much time had gone by from then and whether he had a beard then. I just said that then he did not have a beard, when he came to visit me, and he -- and they asked me whether that was that Boro Milojica, and I didn't say anything that was not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31700 receives number P6966, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Let's turn now to the events in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: This Chamber has received evidence that the Serb forces took over the power in Prijedor in late April 1992. And you know that this happened in Prijedor; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't take over Prijedor. They took the public security station. It was sort of taken over. In Ljubija it wasn't. And I don't know where else there are stations. I was very young then and I was not really very familiar with all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: In your statement, you say at page 2 that on 22 May 1992, you went to the barracks to report to your unit. This Chamber has received evidence that on 20th and 22nd May 1992, Mr. Karadzic and subsequently Prijedor Crisis Staff issued orders on mobilisation, calling all conscripts to report to their units. This is P2872 and P3417. So the reason for you to go to the barracks, Mr. Milojica, was this call for mobilisation; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have already said that I was supposed to go to the front line in Western Slavonia, not for mobilisation, and these other three people who drove us, they're the ones who went for mobilisation. As for Slavonia, there weren't any buses for that, and then they sent us home for an extra two days to rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Did you hear on the newspaper, TV, radio, calling for mobilisation all conscripts to go to their units whenever they were -- and this was happening around 22nd May 1992?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about general mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Let's turn briefly to the shooting at the check-point in Hambarine. You say in your statement that you recognised Aziz Aliskovic and Ferid Delic at the check-point. Shortly after the incident at the check-point, that is in July 1992, Aziz Aliskovic was captured by the Serb forces, killed, and his body was displayed in public. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that he had been killed and that he had been in Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: With respect to Ferid Delic, is it possible that -- that you made a mistake and it was Ferid Sikiric, not Delic. Is it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because Ferid Delic was in our army in Western Slavonia with me and he came on leave together with me and then he crossed over to them, their check-point ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: At page 5 of your statement, you say that they took your rifles at the check-point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it be would fair to put this document on the screen so that the witness can read it. And where on page 5 can we find that portion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: It's D834. We need page 5. And for the B/C/S, it's 4, page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: You said: "They took our papers and rifles to a small house, where they said their command was." Mr. Milojica, this is not correct. In fact, you refused to surrender your weapons; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. Lukic asked them to return us back to barracks, not to touch us, that we were on way home, that we had no intention of doing anything. We also had two Croats with us. In fact this was -- I mean, in Prijedor, until then, the situation was peaceful. That is to say, no one had been killed. There was no excessive behaviour. Everything worked normally. And then quite simply we were frightened, and this Lukic asked for the surrender of weapons and to be returned to barracks. They promised sort of that they would return to us barracks and took our documents and rifles and went to this command to sort of agree on something, and they pointed all their rifles at us and they didn't let us get out of the car at all. And there were six of us in the car, and how could we get out or do anything? Except for the driver, they made him go out and open the trunk.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And when they told you at the check-point to go to the military barracks, you also refused; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not refuse. We were praying to God that they return us to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 31692.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: This is a note made by the SJB Prijedor on interview with Ferid Sikiric on 3 June 1992. And this is what they recorded. "On ... 22 May 1992, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you please direct the witness to the portion you are reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Should be starting paragraph 3. Third paragraph. "On ... 22nd May 1992, I was at the check-point in Hambarine." Then few lines below it says: "Then a civilian vehicle arrived. Security at the check-point stopped the vehicle and Aziz Aliskovic approached the driver who was wearing civilian clothes. The driver then got out of the vehicle and stood next to its open door. There were people in military uniforms sitting on the back seat. Then, I too approached the vehicle ..." Next page in English. "I heard Aliskovic tell the driver that the soldiers did not have the prescribed insignia on their uniforms and that they must leave their weapons and to go to the barracks to see the commander. The soldiers refused to do this and did not want to surrender their weapons, even though the driver tried to persuade them that they would have not any problems because he knew Aziz Aliskovic personally. After the soldiers refused to disarm, the vehicle came under fire. I had the feeling that the shooting was coming from all directions."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Milojica, contrary to your statement, you refused to surrender the weapons and you refused to go to the barracks, and then the incident started at the check-point; right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not right. Not right. One million per cent sure. Everybody has his own story and also we were not all wearing the same thing. There were two Croats who were in civilian clothes and then this third one also who had been mobilised then, he was wearing civilian clothing too. It was only us who wore military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question for the witness. Was it common at the time that when there was no transportation to the front of Western Slavonia, as you've told us, that when sent home again, that you would take your weapons with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, from Western Slavonia. Everybody was told that they could take a rifle, whoever wanted to. However, I was young and I was not very good at this kind of thing. I didn't take one but the other two did. One was older than I was and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it was left to your own free will whether or not to take your weapon, leaving the barracks --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leaving the barracks, going home, whether you want take your rifle or whether you would leave it in the barracks. That was totally unregulated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I left that rifle in Slavonia. I did not bring a rifle from Western Slavonia at all. I mean, at the front line. At the front line. I didn't bring that rifle back at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the others, they had been with you at the front line in Western Slavonia? The others who were with you in the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, those two. Whereas the three people, no, Lulic, Mijatovic, Antunovic, they had been mobilised that day and they were wearing civilian clothes. Let me just tell you one more thing. At that time, we trusted each other so much. I mean, when I trusted Croats to sit together with them, it's just the parties that it started then. None of us were afraid to get into the same car with him because we were neighbours and we respected each other. And then this thing happened at the check-point and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My question was focused on how it happened that some coming from the front line would take their weapons with them and even take them home; whereas you said: I left my weapon at the front line. To whom did you give it? What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there's this place where it's left at the command. I mean, people who don't want to take their weapons, take them along. I had a carbine. It wasn't a good rifle at all, an M48. I didn't want to take it at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it was just left to yourself whether you take your weapon home or whether you leave it in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I mean, weapons --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've answered my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, before we -- I give you an opportunity to re-examine the witness, perhaps we take the break first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes? We'll take a break of 20 minutes, Mr. Milojica, and we'd like to see you back. We resume at ten minutes to 11.00. You can follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you give us any indication as --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I hope I will be finished in 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fifteen, most probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Milojica, you'll now be re-examined by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have on our screens, P6965, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Milojica, we will shortly see a document, and that is a record of your interview of the 21st of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the third page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is noted here above the word "decision" that you have understood the charges and that you would state your defence and give an account of the event and you that would not retain a defence counsel for the time being. After that, the court issued its decision, as is noted here, and appointed Radenko Jankovic as counsel for you. It says that he was a graduate of the law university and not a lawyer. So it's a difference in comparison to the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if there's any translation issue, you bring that to our attention. And to -- hinting at what the difference is between what we read in English and what the witness reads in B/C/S is already not something you would be -- appropriately do. If there is any difference, you should have asked this to be verified instead of telling the witness what it is not. Apparently you were aware of this. You should have told us at the end of the last session. Instead of now putting it to the witness. The witness is not a translator.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can he remove his headphones, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please remove your headphones for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think that he is aware of the difference at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you point it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I cannot say "a lawyer" since it does not say "a lawyer" on this document. That's why I was pointing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then what you could have done, you could just have read it or you could have drawn our attention to a possible translation issue. But you should have done that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will address that man or a person or whatever. I don't think that he can distinguish between those titles in our legal system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But you could have asked him to read that portion into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then we would have the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's clear that you -- Mr. Lukic, that there were no bad attentions when drawing the attention of the witness to differences in the two languages. The witness can put on his earphones again. If you mention Mr. Jankovic that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, would you just kindly read to us what it says in the first paragraph below the word "decision." Can you see that on your screen? I mean, you can come closer to the screen. And can you please read what it says below the word "decision," "rjesenje."

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you read what it says about the defence attorney.

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Radenko Jankovic, a lawyer from Banja Luka, is hereby appointed as assigned counsel to suspect Ratko Milojica."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now it turns out we have received exactly the interpretation --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A lawyer, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- as it is written in the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on. We may have some further comments on it later. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Radojica [sic], before you gave this statement, did you talk with anyone who introduced themselves to you as your legal representative, as your defence attorney in this case?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the last page of the document in both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this page, we can see the signatures of the investigating judge, the court clerk, and the accused. You accepted this -- that this was your signature. After this interview, after it was completed, did you then speak to anybody who introduced themselves as your legal representative or your defence attorney?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know how much you remember today, but -- and tell us only if you remember, did any of these persons who are here, did anybody else -- was anyone else asked to sign this paper; and did they -- if so, did anybody refuse to sign the paper?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was not recorded in the transcript. Could you please repeat your answer. The interpreters didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say anything earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So do you remember today --

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During this entire procedure - the beginning, the middle, and the end - did you ever speak with anybody who was there in the capacity of your legal representative?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at P6966, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a judgement against your relative, Boro Milojica. The Prosecutor put to you that you had come to protect your relative, your cousin, and that you therefore did not tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I would now like to look at page 6 in the English again, please, and page 9 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The following sentence was read to you. It begins at line 10 in the B/C/S version, from the top of the page, and in the English, it's line 5, which says: "The witness emphasised that Boro did not have a beard. He further stated that he did not know anything about the murder of Cehic Rasim. He said that apart from the accused, he did not know of any other Milojica Boro. He stated that he knew that Boro's brother had been killed at the beginning of the war and confirmed that during the period in question, Milojica Boro had been at the unit and at home in the area." And then the court goes on to find: "This testimony also does not undermine testimonies of the prosecution witnesses in any way. Furthermore, as is the case with other defence witnesses, this testimony confirms that the accused was in that area at the critical time-period, that he does not know of any other Boro other than him, and that he does not know anything about the murder of Cehic, Rasim. This witness factually confirms the value of the statements made by the prosecution witnesses as well." You told us today that on the 23rd of July, Boro visited you. Why did he visit you on the 23rd of July?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I had returned from the hospital in Belgrade. He just wanted to see me. He didn't have any news of me for two months because the corridor was closed. So finally I came home. And then all the neighbours came and he came too, to see me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please look at a part of this document in B/C/S that has not been translated. We need page 5, the last paragraph on that page. And, at the bottom, it state -- we need to look at this page so that we can see that this is the testimony by Ljuban Vili. The last two words on this page say: "This witness ..." So can we now look at the next page, please, "... describes that with the arrival in front of the house of Cehic Rasim, some soldiers searched the house. They didn't find weapons, that the same -- the person in question was a civilian but that they took out of the house bills, kunas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zec, you were on your feet. Is there any objection against Mr. Lukic reading at this moment or is it ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: As far as I can see where it goes, it seems like it's beyond the scope of my cross. So I was trying to alert the Court [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, no, you have drawn the attention of the role of this witness in those proceedings, and Mr. Lukic may further explore that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question, since it is all about visiting and whether having a beard or not, and perhaps that comes back, but what was the date exactly on which the crime charged would have taken place?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's 14th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do the parties agree on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: August 1992. And the visit was on 23rd of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that there is no dispute about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will continue to read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you do, Mr. Lukic, is there any hope that we'll get a translation of this part that's not translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document was uploaded by the Prosecution. And we will ask for this portion to be translated as well, yes, Your Honour. But now that's why I'm reading now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, I understand. I'm just hoping that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm hoping too. Then I will continue to read. [Interpretation] "Once they arrived in front of the house of Rasim Cehic, some soldiers searched the house. They did not find any weapons, that the person in question was a civilian, but that they took out of the house bank-notes, kunas, from World War II, and that a quarrel broke out between the accused and Rasim Cehic. He was standing some 10 metres away from them, and he saw Boro firing one shot from a sniper rifle into Rasim Cehic who fell, and then he personally cursed Boro, telling him that 'that is not okay' and that the other person responded 'they killed my brother.'"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your testimony in the Karadzic case and in your testimony today, did you confirm that the brother of your cousin Boro Milojica was killed? If you remember. Radovan.

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when was Radovan killed?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 22nd of May, when I was wounded and all the others too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we just quickly look at 65 ter 31692.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently we have here a judgement which is not fully translated. One, if -- one of the issues that apparently appear is whether the witness said that "he had no beard when he visited me" or a time, because in the judgement, the part that is translated, it is referred to this witness saying something about at the -- if I could say so, the relevant time. Now if there is any other portion of this judgement which gives more details about the statement of the witness, in that case, then I think the parties should try to find that together and submit that for translation as well. If it sheds any light on what exactly the witness testified in this case, apart from the evaluation of that evidence by the court at the end. Again, I do not know whether there's anything more in it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't think so, Your Honour. I read the judgement and there is nothing more specific --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Is there -- apart from the judgement, is there a transcript or a report of the hearing which, of course, may exist which might shed more light on what the witness exactly stated there? Which would certainly assist the Chamber in the evaluation of what is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There must be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So if the parties could try to find that and then to provide the Chamber with more details about the witness testified. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think -- I think it could be a joint effort by both parties. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last document, Mr. Milojica, was this one, I mean, the one that was shown to you by my colleague, which is an Official Note, in terms of what Sikiric Ferid stated on the 3rd of June, 1992, at the public security station in Prijedor. In order not to lead, let me ask you this way: Since it was put to you that there was a difference between Mr. Sikiric's statement and your own as to whether you had handed over your weapon or not, on that occasion, did anyone from your car open fire at the people who were at the check-point?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. With 100 per cent certainty, no. There was no chance for us to fire. There were four of us sitting in the back seat all over each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us see the bottom of the page. We need the last line in B/C/S. In English version, we need page 3. And we need in English, fourth line from the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sikiric is explaining where the people at the check-point were around the car and this is what he says. Do you see the last down -- the last line down here?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, we need the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "When the vehicle was checked, there were two men in front of the vehicle, two men at the back. Aziz was to the left of the driver and I was to the right of the vehicle. I was on the side, looking from the direction of the check-point breastwork." How many of you were sitting on the back seat of the car?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we -- could I ask: What kind of a car was it? Golf. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I intervened. I spoke too quickly. Could you repeat what you said about the car.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Golf Kec, as we called it. It is Golf number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just like to show another exhibit from the list provided by the Prosecution yesterday and today, 65 ter 20016, and it has to do with your responsibility. This is a document of the military court in Banja Luka dated the 25th of February, 1994, and this is a decision taken by this court. And it says here that the charges are dropped against Boro Milojica, Ranko Karan, and Ratko Milojica, all from Prijedor. Did you ever receive this document?

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask a question here. The interpretation said: "The charges are dropped." The writing says: "Suspended." What is the correct one? There's a difference between those two.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Dropped. That's my understanding. "Suspended" means that something can be continued. After this decision, this proceeding cannot be continued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking the question because of precisely that difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I have to testify because I don't think that the witness can testify on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, I was asking the interpreters to help us.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We repeat what we have said: Charges have been dropped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As to the legal meaning of that - and, Mr. Zec, I'm also addressing you - if you -- Mr. Zec, I'm also drawing your attention to it. If the parties could agree on what it actually in legal terms means, dropping, whether that's dropping forever or only on a temporary basis, then, of course, that would be appreciated if you would stipulate on the meaning of it. Apart from the linguistic translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But I note for the record, under the heading "Explanation," in the last two lines it was -- it can be read that the prosecutor's office was withdrawing the indictment and therefore the proceedings are suspended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly the reason why I asked the parties to seek agreement on what the -- what the legal status of the accused would have been after this decision. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would tender this document into the evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 20016 receives number D835, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I don't know if it -- if I did not jot it down or if the Prosecution omitted to offer 31692 into the evidence. It was not tendered yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It was not tendered yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then we would tender that document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would like to make it a D exhibit or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If the Prosecution [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or if Mr. Zec forgot about it, you might be so generous as to still make a P exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then, yeah, let's make it P, if my learned friend wants --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: My understanding that is the statement of this Sikiric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I read the relevant portion but I don't have objection if the counsel wants the whole document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If you say you -- on purpose you only limited it. Perhaps for context it is better to have the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's not a long one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in evidence. In view of your generous offer, Mr. Lukic, and since Mr. Zec addressed the matter first, let's make it a P exhibit. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31692 receives number P6967, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And I will just thank to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milojica, we have no further questions for you. Thank you for having answered our questions.

utterances.speaker: RATKO MILOJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Bench has no further questions. Mr. Zec, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Milojica, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you. You are excused. You may follow the usher. And I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could the next witness could be escorted into the courtroom. If at least the Defence is ready. The Defence is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No loud speaking. No loud speaking. If you want to consult, take off your earphones and consult with counsel. At whispering volume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Sajic, I presume. Mr. Sajic, before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Sajic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sajic, you will first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. I find Mr. Stojanovic to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic. If you switch on your microphone, we could ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please speak slowly for the transcript and give us your name and surname.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I am Milorad Sajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sajic, at one point in time, did you give the Defence of Radovan Karadzic a written statement?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have 65 ter 1D02520 in e-court. I would also like to ask that we take a look at the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sajic, on this last page of the document that we saw or, rather, we had seen its first page, the date, is it written in your hand?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now take a look at paragraph 1 of your statement. In your CV, Mr. Sajic, during the proofing that we had before you appeared in this courtroom, did you not tell me that in B/C/S -- as far as I understood things, it's not really a problem in the English version, but in B/C/S - and you insisted on this - it said: I have a degree in economics and I am a teacher of national defence. And you say that it would be more appropriate if it were to state: In terms of my education, I'm an economist and a professor of national defence. Would that be more appropriate and more correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could we now take a look at paragraph 53 of your statement. Mr. Sajic, as we were going through these documents during the proofing, did you indicate to me that in paragraph 53, there's a word - this is a resolution of the ARK Executive Council and it's supposed to say "rjesenje," a decision?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now that we've carried out these two corrections, in terms of what you had indicated to us, today, in this courtroom, now that you've taken the solemn declaration that you will say the truth and nothing but the truth, do you fully stand by the statement that you gave to the Defence of Mr. Karadzic, and would that constitute your truthful testimony to the best of your knowledge about the matters that you had been asked?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender the witness's statement into evidence, 1D250. The statement of witness Milorad Sajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, no objection. Mr. Stojanovic, the witness comments, I think, on many adjudicated facts, isn't it? Are those adjudicated facts from this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. And we provided a table of the markings and the numbers of adjudicated facts to the Prosecution, but it was numbered according to the system from our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now that's fine that the Prosecution is informed about such a table. The Chamber is finally the authority which have to evaluate this evidence. Let me just have a look. Is that for the adjudicated facts, is that the case? I mean, for the associated exhibits that's perhaps different, but, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I might assist, Mr. President. I think Mr. Stojanovic is referring to a table which has been uploaded into e-court under 65 ter 1D05304 and he -- we'd asked the Defence if they were going to be tendering something making that connection. My understanding was that they did intend to tender that table in the context of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is it on your list of associated exhibits? I'm just looking, where is it, under what number exactly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When was it put on your list, Mr. Stojanovic? I see six associated exhibits if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which one of it is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None of these six. These are additional ones and that was uploaded into e-court by our assistant yesterday. And we would like to put some questions about the documents to our witness today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'm talking about adjudicated facts primarily, not about documents. Are they phrased in exactly the same way in the Karadzic case as they were in our case? Because I see that there's a reference, for example, to 539. Of course, I noticed that we have no adjudicated fact under number 539 so -- but have you carefully compared whether the -- whether the phrasing of the adjudicated facts in the Karadzic corresponds for the full 100 per cent with adjudicated facts in our case?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we did check that, and we think so, yes, and we think that that adjudicated fact from the Karadzic case, 539, should correspond fully to our adjudicated fact 431.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's have a look then. Because it may be true that the Prosecution is fully aware of all this, but as matters stand now, the Chamber is not informed about it. And you said it was 431. Let's just have a look at it. Yes, that, at least ... yes, it seems to be literally the same. Of course, you have checked that for all the adjudicated facts, that they are literally the same. And that table, do you intend to tender that right away or -- so that we at least know what we are admitting?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could you please -- I mentioned the number of that table. And could we just have it on our screens for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see it's there. Is there any objection against admission of that table? If there's not, Madam Registrar, could you provide numbers, first, for the statement of the witness and then, second, for the table of concordance.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2520 receives number D386. And document 1D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Is it 386?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D386, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Not 836? 836.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 836. My apologies, D836.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D836 is admitted into evidence. And now the table of concordance.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D5304 receives number D837, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D837 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would also like to tender six documents and I would also like to read out all six of them, if you think that would be more efficient. I would read out the 65 ter numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we tender document 65 ter 1D02940, which corresponds to paragraph 19 of the witness statement. Then 1D02984, which corresponds to paragraph 32 of the witness statement. Then 1D023810 [as interpreted], which corresponds to paragraph 44 of the witness statement. The next document is 1D02384, which corresponds to paragraph 53 of the witness statement. The next document is 65 ter number 1D -- it is actually 04847, which corresponds to paragraph 41 of the witness statement. And, finally, document which has the number 17 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- for paragraph - let me just have a look -

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think you misread, Mr. Stojanovic. The last one was 65 ter 9847. And you said 4847. Please check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The 65 ter number is 09847.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- the numbers are ... we have -- you said six documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. And the last one is number 17009, which corresponds to paragraph 62 of the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now there's one document where I still have some problems. That is, in relation to paragraph 44. Let me just check. It reads on the transcript "1D023810," and I take it that it should be 1D02310.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, could you assign numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2940 receives number D838. Document 1D2984 receives number D839. Document 1D2310 receives number D840. Document 1D2384 receives number D841. Document 9847 receives number D842. And document 17009 receives number D843, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D838 up to and including D843 are admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to read a short summary of the statement of Witness Milorad Sajic, with your leave, Your Honours. Witness Milorad Sajic was a professor of national defence until the war and also performed the duty of the commander of the TO of the municipality of Banja Luka during the spring and summer of 1992. At the same time he was also carrying out the duties of the secretary of the regional Secretariat for National Defence. At the same time he was also a member of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of the Krajina, and he was an officer of the VRS by the end of the war. In his statement, he speaks about the organisation and functioning of the Territorial Defence, about the reorganisation of the TO units and their transformation into units which after the 12th of May, 1992, became part of the newly formed VRS. He states that this task of reorganising the units required time as well as the establishment of commands of the newly formed brigades so that the entire job was completed by mid-June 1992. He will describe in detail his duties as secretary of the Secretariat of National Defence in the Autonomous Region of the Krajina. Then his personal knowledge relating to arming through both illegal and legal channels when the call-up was announced and how the weapons were distributed both to the Muslim and Croatian communities in keeping with the declared mobilisation. He will speak about his knowledge about the Serbian defence forces and the blockades of Banja Luka in April 1992, about the work of the Crisis Staff of the ARK, the relationship between the Crisis Staff and the Army of Republika Srpska, claiming that the military structure was never placed under the control of civilian authorities. He is aware of the decision of the ARK Crisis Staff about the disarming of paramilitary formations and how the same applied to all paramilitary formations regardless of the ethnic group which formed them. He will speak about his experiences relating to the position of the Pale authorities in relation to the ARK and will state how the strategic objectives stated at a session of the SRBiH Assembly never intended as their goal to expel Muslims or Croats from the territory of the RS. He had the opportunity to meet General Mladic on the 12th of May, 1992, at the Assembly of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and to be present during his contacts and while he was stating his position in relation to Defence Minister Subotic. Finally, he will comment on eight adjudicated facts and explain why he believed that they do not correspond to the actual situation on the ground and his information about the situation in the field. Your Honour, that was the summary. I'm looking at the clock, and I think that after the break, I would put a few questions to the witness and thereby finish my part in today's proceedings in relation to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. We'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher. And we will resume at 20 minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please have document D836 in e-court, and I'd like to focus on paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sajic, I'm just going to put a question to you in order to clarify your statement. The last two sentences in paragraph 2 of your statement where you say -- can you see that now? "I was a member of the Crisis Staff of the AR Krajina and in the same year, 1992, I became an officer of the VRS ..." I'd like you to tell the Court until when were you practically within the Crisis Staff of the ARK and from when did you join the VRS as an officer?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I was secretary of the Secretariat for National Defence until, say, the end of July, and in the beginning of August as a reserve lieutenant-colonel, I went to the front in Slavonia -- or, rather, I went to Posavina, and I was a member of the Crisis Staff ex officio. So, in the beginning of August, I became an officer of the Army of Republika Srpska. After 1996, I was a director of the Palace Hotel, and so on and so forth. That is to say, I was demobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you please tell the Trial Chamber in practical terms where you were stationed from August 1992 in Posavina with the unit that you belonged to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
