utterances.text: First, for a while, I was in the territory of Posavina or, more specifically, the municipality of Zabari nowadays, and later on in Brod, Derventa, Tactical Group 3. That's where I was until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now take a look at paragraph 14 of your statement. In order to clarify. This is what you say: "In April 1992, I became the secretary of the Secretariat of National Defence of the Autonomous Region of the Krajina." Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what happened with the duty that you carried out until then, the commander of the TO Staff of Banja Luka? Did you continue to exercise these duties?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I was commander of the TO Staff in Banja Luka until the 15th or 16th of July, when brigades were established from the personnel of the TO. That was my professional duty. I was paid for that. It was a paid job. As for being secretary of the secretariat for the region of the AR Krajina, I was appointed to that position, I think, towards the end of April. I can't remember the date. But this duty, secretary of the Secretariat of the AR Krajina, I did that in addition to being head of the TO, commander of the TO. This was a professional thing. Also, I was not paid later as secretary of the secretariat but, rather, as an employee or official of the municipality of Banja Luka until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please take a look at paragraph 56 now, 56 of your statement. You speak of your impressions here from the meetings of the Crisis Staff or, rather, the discussions that were held then. And you refer to an official whose last name is Radic. And then in the second sentence, you say: "Radic was sitting at the back and he gave an answer that did not satisfy them." Please could you clarify what you meant by that, "Radic was sitting in the back"?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: In the room where this meeting was held on that day, there were meetings on other days too, but on that day, Radic was sitting further away from me, and then for me that meant in the back. So I was sort of here, and he was sort of there. So I see that as in the back of the room, the premises there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now paragraph 52, please, paragraph 52 of your statement, where you speak about the situation when you had the opportunity to hear and see the contact that General Mladic had. And, please, without repeating what is written here, could you tell us what was actually the reason for this reaction of Mr. Mladic's vis-à-vis Mr. Subotic and what was your conclusion on that basis?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: This was during the break while the assembly was in session. I was not at that session until the end, but General Mladic was sitting there, General Talic, and I. During the break, Subotic walked up to us --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could Mr. Stojanovic please turn off his microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So he was explaining to General Talic that certain status-related questions would be resolved --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead, Mr. Witness. I was just supposed to switch off my own microphone.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: So he was explaining some status-related questions for him and for officers. Mr. Mladic then said that he would not interfere in that. He was very explicit. He said that it was not his business. Actually, this was a reflection of his attitude. He was man who knew that as far as command is concerned, that he was responsible for all of those who were below him, and he was very strict, very stern. He asked for fairness, and he asked for people not to interfere in the business of others. So that was my impression, that he was the commander of the Main Staff, and that he was responsible for his officers and that he would not be interfering in anything else. That is the way I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Minister Subotic, when he addressed General Talic this way, and when he went over Talic's -- over Mladic's head, did you understand that as an attempt made by Subotic to take over the powers that did he not have in actual fact?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think there's a bit of comment in the question, and I'd ask that it be rephrased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please do that. Apart from there being comment in it, I've not often heard a question more leading than this one. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, what was the reaction of Subotic at that moment?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: My impression was that General Subotic practically spoke about a subject that was not within the scope of his work. He was minister, but all officers were responsible to General Mladic. So he was not supposed to interfere in that. And then during the break, no one spoke to anyone else and then the assembly continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sajic, for these answers. At this point in time, for the time being we have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for this time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask a question. The last answer you gave, Mr. Sajic, starts with, as it is recorded: "My impression was that General Subotic practically spoke about a subject" matter, and so on, did you really say "General Subotic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I could have said just "Subotic." He was a colonel then. I don't think he was a general yet. Colonel. Later on, he did become a general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Was he, at that point, in time minister?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Because in your statement, you are addressing him as "minister" and not with a military rank. I'm talking about Mr. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Subotic was in Banja Luka as a colonel, and he went to Pale as a colonel. I don't know when he became minister, but at that time he was a colonel. In the hierarchy, a colonel is always below a general. But he was a colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's clear. But in paragraph 52 of your statement, you are addressing him as "Minister Subotic." And was he present during this conversation in his capacity as minister or as a military man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He wore the uniform of a colonel then. Whether he was a minister, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't sure. Later on, he would become -- well, maybe this was a slip in the statement. But anyway, he wore the uniform of a colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take that the parties could find agreement on whether -- when Mr. Subotic became minister of defence? Do you have already an opinion about it, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's wait until Mr. Stojanovic is listening in again. Yes, Mr. Traldi, in the view of the Prosecution, Mr. Subotic became a minister when?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't have a date for appointment. I would say it is our position that he had become minister before the 12th of May, 1992, and also no later than the 16th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There two things. I see Mr. Stojanovic nodding yes and I see Mr. Mladic waving with his finger which suggests a no. So, therefore -- but I have one question for you. Just assuming that he was a minister, you explained to us, you said -- and I take ... one second, please. I find your -- you said: "My impression was that Mr. Subotic practically spoke about a subject that was not within the scope of his work." Now, is the organisation of the financing of an army, is that not within the scope of the work of a minister of defence? Just assuming that he was a minister already.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The organisation of financing the army in a country is within the purview of minister's job, but in our situation it was a bit distorted, if I can put it that way. You have a situation when a colonel becomes a minister and the commander of the Main Staff is a general. I'm trying to say that this gesture that was made at that moment, during that break, by Subotic who addressed Talic, General Talic, who is there before his commander, General Mladic, that was ill-advised, to put it mildly. Because the commander of the Main Staff -- that is my understanding of the situation and I think that's only natural. The commander of the Main Staff is responsible before all for all of his officers. He commands them and he is responsible for all of them. So it was his view that it was his business, not Subotic's. That was my understanding, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, to say that it becomes clear, your statement says that he talked to General Talic about the organisation of the VRS financing and you tell us that that is within the purview of the task of a minister but, nevertheless, it was not under those circumstances. That's at least not exactly what your statement says and that is not fully in line with what you said earlier, that he practically spoke about the subject that was not within the scope of his work, whereas you now say it was but it was slightly different. Let's move on. Mr. Traldi, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before -- one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Judge Moloto would like to address you briefly, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you start, Mr. Traldi, if you can look at page 53, lines 14 to 16, and check whether the dates are 146th of May and 124th of April. And having done so, my question to you, you said by the 24th May he had become a minister but no later than April. Do you want to say no earlier than April 14th?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. What I had intended to say it was our position is that he had become minister before the 12th of May, which was the date of the 16th Assembly that was being discussed, and also no later than the 16th of April, so not later than the 16th of April, which was the first date I had immediately to mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Traldi, please, start your cross-examination of the witness. Mr. Sajic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You'll find him to your right, and Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you testified before this Tribunal in the Brdjanin case; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Also the Karadzic case; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I take it it's your position that you told the truth in those testimonies; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You were also interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor in 2001. Did you tell the truth in that interview?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Even though I never actually saw the statement, I just signed it. It was an audio recording.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Actually, could we have 65 ter 31671.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This will be part of your testimony in the Brdjanin case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm looking for page 23, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is the very beginning of your cross-examination in the Brdjanin case and the prosecuting counsel is asking you very similar questions. But beginning in line 17, he asks: "And I think I read in your statement to the Defence ..." I'm going to pause there. You also gave a statement to the Brdjanin Defence; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so Mr. Nicholls asks: "I think I read in your statement to the Defence that you had reviewed a portion of the transcript in your language from your interview with the OTP, and you confirmed that your words had been faithfully recorded; correct?" You answered: "Yes. But maybe there were some mistranslations. On the whole, though, that is true."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, but we don't have a translation. Ever since Mr. Traldi began, we don't have -- we're not hearing the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you indicate from where exactly. Because if is the whole of the questioning where Mr. Traldi -- then, I'm a bit surprised that you report it only now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the whole question, from the moment when Mr. Traldi started quoting from line 17 of the transcript in the Brdjanin case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please resume from there, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, can you confirm that you're receiving translation of what I'm saying now?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. I'd ask two questions about that. First, you gave a statement to the Brdjanin Defence; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And at line 17 here, Mr. Nicholls is asking you about that statement and says: "And I think I read in your statement to the Defence that you had reviewed a portion of the transcript in your language from your interview with the OTP, and you confirmed that your words had been faithfully recorded; correct?" And you responded: "Yes. But maybe there were some mistranslations. On the whole, though, that is true." And following up on that question, the Prosecutor asked you: "Yes, well, from what you read, you said that everything had been faithfully recorded; right?" And you answered: "Yes."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I don't see the statement on my screen. I see it in English. And on the basis of this statement, you are concluding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Traldi is not concluding anything at this moment. Mr. Traldi is asking questions. And he puts to you your testimony in the Brdjanin case which is available only in English, and therefore he slowly reads it so that you can hear what the questions were at the time and what your answers were at the time. It may that be Mr. Traldi later moves to the statement you've given. Wait for that. And listen carefully to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm putting to you at the moment is: Previously today, at temporary transcript page 56, I asked: "You were also interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor in 2001." You confirmed that you had told the truth in that interview but then you said you never actually saw a statement. And so for the clarity of the record, what I'm putting to you is that in your truthful testimony in the Brdjanin case, you confirmed that you had, in fact, reviewed a transcript of the interview you had with the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A portion is what --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: A portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you then please phrase it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you did review a portion of that transcript; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to move off this topic now and I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play a short clip which has been uploaded as 65 ter 22341A. And actually I'm going to ask that we freeze right at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Mr. Traldi, I want one thing to be very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Sajic, when you gave that statement to the Office of the Prosecution, irrespective of whether you had an opportunity to review the whole of it and irrespective of whether you make a reservation as far as possible translation errors may have occurred, at that time when you gave that statement, did you intend to tell the truth? And did you, to your recollection, tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear. Because what you said is still available on audio and how it is transcribed and how it is translated is also still available for verification if there would be any problem in relation to that. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And just to be clear, we won't be relying on any audio for the clip that I'm using.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, we've frozen at the beginning of the clip. Can you tell us who the three people we see there in the front row are?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't -- yes, there it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Mladic, Talic, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this is at the 16th Session of the Republika Srpska Assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could play up to 8 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person we see seated to General Mladic's right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did members of the authorities from the SAO Krajina in Croatia attend this session?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: It looks like Hadzic to me. If that's what you are thinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's Goran Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: It looks like him, but I -- I can't be sure. And I don't know if they attended or not. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could play up to 25 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who do we see on our screen now?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What was Mr. Milovanovic's first name?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I think he was the vice-president. He was a doctor by profession, but I can't remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mr. Krajisnik is Momcilo Krajisnik, the president of the assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Momcilo Krajisnik, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could play up to 48 seconds and then pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the man on the right side of the image, you'd been unsure before. Are you able to identify him now?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: It looks like Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just to ensure my chronology is correct, by this point, he was the president of the RSK; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the man with white hair at the end of the second row?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Perhaps this is Ivanstanin from Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could play forwards to 55 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's President Karadzic, right, in the front row?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And up to 1 minute, 3 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And who is sitting next to him in uniform?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Behind President Karadzic, do you recognise the face of the man with the moustache?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: It looks like Martic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is that Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if you look two seats to Mr. Martic's right, do you recognise the man seated there in a white shirt and a tie?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could play up to 1 minute, 16 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the three people we see here?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I recognise Velibor Ostojic, in the middle. I cannot remember the person to the left or to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'd ask that we go ahead to 1 minute, 55 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the man in the front with his finger on his lips?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, I'd tender 65 ter 22341A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm just waiting for a CD. Thank you. Document 22341A receives number P6968, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, a seat in the front row next to General Talic and General Mladic at an event like this would have been reserved for a person of some importance; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: No, I -- I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me ask it this way. The people you've identified in the front row are presidents, ministers, generals, and yourself, and you were not at that time a president, a minister of the RS, or a general. What about your various positions qualified you for a seat in the front row on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Nothing qualified me. I think that the general said: Here, sit there. It was not a seat assigned to me. And they were all all over the hall, if I can put that way. The seats were scattered.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Which general told you to sit there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I think that it was General Mladic. I approached General Talic. He explained to General Mladic who I was, what I was, and he said: Well, just take a seat here. But I didn't actually have a seat that was pre-assigned to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You knew General Talic by this point; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I had heard of him, about him from some reports, and that was the time when I get to know -- got to know him a bit better.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, if he explained to General Mladic who you were and what you were, he clearly knew you too; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I don't believe that General Mladic could have known me from before. There were no contacts. There was no reason for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, let me ask the question very precisely. You testified that General Talic explained to General Mladic who you were and what you were. To do that, it must be the case that General Talic knew you. It wasn't merely the case that you were familiar with him from reports; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I don't understand or perhaps the translation I received was not accurate. In any case, General Talic knew me; General Mladic did not know me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You explained that "that was the time when I got to know him a bit better," referring to General Talic. That period is May and June 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: No. I explained that that was the occasion when I met General Mladic and got to know him a little bit better, not General Talic. I knew General Talic from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. You remained at this assembly session through General Mladic's speech; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I don't think I attended the entire assembly session. Perhaps I can say when I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let me ask the question again. You remained long enough that you heard General Mladic speak; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that. I -- I can't remember. I left at the break. I think it was perhaps the second break, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence that the first speaker was President Karadzic. So you were there for his speech; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were aware, then, of the strategic objectives that he set out at this session; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I cannot be sure anymore, whether I heard about the strategic goals then or if I left before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you stayed till the second break, you said a moment ago. President Karadzic spoke first. Is it your evidence that the president of the republic is laying out the people's strategic objectives, you're sitting in the front row, and you might not have understood or might have become distracted?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: My answer would be perhaps I did listen to it, but I can't remember it. I don't recall those goals, objectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, you can accept, sitting there, that separation of Serbs from Muslim and Croats was one of the strategic goals that President Karadzic laid out; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's have 65 ter 31672, page 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm calling this up, sir, because you have accepted that in your testimony in the Brdjanin case. So you'd been asked about the strategic goals and you'd answered at the top of the page: "I know that they were presented, those goals were presented. I know that there was mention of those goals."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I'm not getting the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you now receive interpretation? Do you hear my words now? Could you please repeat your question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, at the top of the page you're testifying and you say: "I know they were presented, those goals were presented. I know that there was mention of those goals." So when you testified in the Brdjanin case, you agreed that you knew that the strategic objectives were presented at that time. Can you confirm today that you know the strategic objectives were presented at the 16th Session of the Republika Srpska Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was something that was known even by those who were not present at the assembly session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then the prosecuting counsel is reading to you from the transcript of that assembly and he says: "All right. Let me refresh your memory." He says: "This is President Krajisnik speaking."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this can be found -- the quote that he is referring to can be found on page 9 of P431. We're not obviously relying on the previous counsel's depiction of the speaker.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It says: "'The Serbian side of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Presidency, the government, the Council for National Security which we have set up have formulated strategic priorities, that is to say, the strategic goals for the Serbian people. The first such goal is separation from the other two national communities, the separation of state, separation from those who are our enemies and who have used every opportunity, especially in this century, to attack us, and who would continue with such practices if we were to continue to stay together in the same state.'" "That's strategic goal number 1. Do you remember hearing that now?" And you responded that you could accept that it had been said. And then at line 17 you said: "I can accept that this was a strategic goal. I'm not denying that." Do you today accept that this was one of the strategic goals that was laid out at the 16th Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right. I want to turn now to some other meetings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I'm looking at the clock. If we turn to another subject, would this be an appropriate moment to take a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It would for me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Sajic, we take another break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at 25 minutes to 2.00. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I asked you to confirm that the adjudicated facts in the Karadzic case as given in the statement are for 100 per cent exactly the same as the adjudicated facts in our case. There are serious reasons to believe that despite your confirmation that they are not exactly the same, although -- therefore, could you have a close look at what is 421 in our case and what is 447. Verify that and inform the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not saying that they are not accurate in the table of concordance, but at least there are a few problems which were noted by the Chamber's staff. And, of course, we couldn't do it any earlier because we were not provided with the table that you have provided to us now. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before we start back up, during the break, Mr. Stojanovic and I spoke. We're agreed that the speaker setting out the first strategic objective at the 16th Assembly was President Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And could we have 65 ter 31672, page 11, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to finish the last topic, sir, your attendance at the 16th Assembly and when you were there. Beginning in line 17 you're being asked about something particular that Mr. Brdjanin said there. At line 25, you say: "No. As I said before, I did not" - and then it continues on the next page - "attend the whole meeting. I was there when General Mladic spoke ..." So I put to you again you remained at the session through General Mladic's speech; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I don't have translation into Serbian here, but I did understand what you were saying. I'm not sure that I heard all of Mladic's remarks. Even when I said this, I wasn't sure. But then I don't know what all of this really means.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to another meeting in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit P353, page 53 in the English and the B/C/S transcript. Sir, as it comes up in, in paragraph 45 of your statement, you say: "It had also been planned that Krajisnik, Karadzic, Koljevic, Subotic, and Mladic would hold talks with representatives of the ARK in Banja Luka in late May 1992. But that did not materialise either." Now, in fact, Karadzic and Mladic came to Banja Luka on the 2nd of June, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know when the two of them came but this meeting that had been planned was not held. I can't remember when it was that Karadzic and Mladic came to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, we're looking here at a page of General Mladic's notebook. We see: Banja Luka, 2 June 1992, meeting with leaderships of Banja Luka, Bosnian Krajina, SRK and unit commanders of the 1st Krajina Corps and the commander of the ViPvo of the SRBiH. We see that Karadzic speaks first at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we turn to page 54 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see Mr. Brdjanin speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We still do not see it in English. There it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turn to page 56 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the bottom we see someone named Martic; correct? And then turning to page 57, Vojo Kupresanin. So what Mladic is recording here is a meeting he and President Karadzic had in Banja Luka at the beginning of June 1992 with individuals, including many of the ARK authorities; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I see that that is written here, but I did not attend that meeting. And I don't even know about this meeting. This is the first I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 06923.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an issue of "Oslobodjenje" dated the 3rd of June, 1992, and second one down on the left in the B/C/S, second note, we see Karadzic and Mladic fly to Banja Luka. And we see in the second paragraph that it's been associated with a request by Radoslav Brdjanin to establish the borders of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. So, in fact, this visit was covered in the press at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I didn't read that. And I don't know. I see that there was this reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 06923.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6923 receives number P6969, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, before we leave the topic of meetings, sir, I want to ask briefly about the meeting you had in Knin in May 1992 where you went by helicopter. You discussed this in paragraph 47 of your statement. You, Mr. Brdjanin, Mr. Zupljanin, Mr. Vukic, Mr. Kupresanin, and Mr. Erceg were in Knin to meet with members of the RSK leadership; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Which members of the RSK leadership did your delegation meet with?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I didn't meet with anyone. That is one thing. Brdjanin, I think, met with Martic or I don't know who. And for me, that meeting -- well, later on it turned out to be something political but I did not really understand it. I did not take part in the talks with the AR Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to ask now some questions about the Banja Luka district TO Staff. The command post of the district TO Staff was in the same building as the corps command of what was initially the 5th Corps of the JNA; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your commander, Colonel Spasojevic, had his office in that same building; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your headquarters for the municipal TO Staff was in a municipal building across from the brewery; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Including Banja Luka, there were 14 municipalities with Territorial Defences that were underneath the Banja Luka District Territorial Defence; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: At that moment, at that moment, I think, yes, but before, there were -- there were more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In paragraph 13 of your statement, you say: "The combat engagements of TO units was within the exclusive purview of the JNA." The combat engagement of these units became under the exclusive purview of the VRS after the 19th of May, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, after the brigade was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you describe the reorganisation of the TO into light brigades in paragraphs 11 and 12 of your statement. That required you to meet and speak with General Talic, the 1st Krajina Corps commander; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I did meet with Talic to discuss that matter, so the answer would be yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Among other things, you would propose commanders for the brigades but the corps commander, General Talic, was actually in charge of appointing them; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to the ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And could we have Exhibit P3984, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a list of phone numbers for members of the Krajina Autonomous Region War Staff, what's being described as the War Staff, and it's dated 6th of May, 1992, and signed for Mr. Brdjanin. Are the members reflected correctly here? Sorry, I've been recorded to say "numbers," but I intended to say "members" of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: These are those people but it's not a war-time staff. It was the Crisis Staff. These notions are -- I mean -- I mean, I think that whoever wrote this -- well, I mean, there was never a war-time staff of the AR Krajina. There was a Crisis Staff that was established with these people, Brdjanin, Sajic, Kupresanin, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Traldi, if you move to another subject, there's another subject which I need to address briefly in private session again, so then we already -- no, we couldn't adjourn in private session, so therefore it's good that we first went into open session. Mr. Sajic, we'll adjourn for the day soon, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom. But before you follow the usher, I would like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given already or whether that is testimony still to be given tomorrow. If that's clear to you, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 3rd of December, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 3rd day of December, 2014, at 9.30 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
